```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind, f_oneway
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Men_with_alcohol_abuse_show_greater_cortical_thinn_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Alcohol_abuse_clinically_significant_occurring_over_a_12month_period_manifested_in_one_of_the_following_areas_work_driving_legal_or_social",
    "Subjects_sex"
]

missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
print(df[required_columns].isnull().sum())

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Validate sex categories (assume 0 = female, 1 = male, 2 = other)
sex_categories = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].unique()
print(f"\nUnique sex values: {sex_categories}")

# Check for invalid or out-of-range sex codes
invalid_sex = df_clean[(df_clean["Subjects_sex"] < 0) | (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] > 2)]
if len(invalid_sex) > 0:
    print(f"Warning: Invalid sex codes detected ({len(invalid_sex)} rows). These entries will be removed.")
    df_clean = df_clean[(df_clean["Subjects_sex"] >= 0) & (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] <= 2)]

# Confirm valid sex groupings
sex_groups = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].value_counts()
print(f"\nSex distribution after filtering:\n{sex_groups}")

# Check if both men and women are present
if df_clean["Subjects_sex"].eq(1).sum() == 0:
    print("Error: No male participants (sex == 1) found. Cannot compare men and women.")
    exit()

if df_clean["Subjects_sex"].eq(0).sum() == 0:
    print("Warning: No female participants (sex == 0) found. Correlation or comparison with women cannot proceed.")

# Filter participants with clinically significant alcohol abuse
abuse_mask = df_clean["Alcohol_abuse_clinically_significant_occurring_over_a_12month_period_manifested_in_one_of_the_following_areas_work_driving_legal_or_social"] == 1
df_abuse = df_clean[abuse_mask].copy()

# Ensure we have at least 5 observations in each group
men_with_abuse = df_abuse[df_abuse["Subjects_sex"] == 1]
women_with_abuse = df_abuse[df_abuse["Subjects_sex"] == 0]

if len(men_with_abuse) < 5 or len(women_with_abuse) < 5:
    print("Error: Insufficient sample size in one or both groups with alcohol abuse. Cannot perform reliable comparison.")
    exit()

# Check if cortical thinning data exists — it must be present in the dataset
if "Cortical_thickness" not in df_clean.columns and "Gray_matter_density" not in df_clean.columns:
    print("Error: No cortical thinning or gray matter density variable found in the dataset. Hypothesis cannot be tested.")
    exit()

# Assume cortical thinning is measured as a continuous variable; use "Cortical_thickness" or equivalent
thickness_col = "Cortical_thickness"
if thickness_col not in df_clean.columns:
    print(f"Warning: '{thickness_col}' not found. Using 'Gray_matter_density' instead.")
    thickness_col = "Gray_matter_density"

# If thickness variable still missing, fail
if thickness_col not in df_clean.columns:
    print("Error: Critical variable for cortical thinning or gray matter density is missing. Cannot proceed.")
    exit()

# Extract cortical thinning values for men and women with alcohol abuse
men_thickness = men_with_abuse[thickness_col]
women_thickness = women_with_abuse[thickness_col]

# Perform independent t-test comparing cortical thinning between men and women with alcohol abuse
try:
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(men_thickness, women_thickness, equal_var=False)
    print(f"\nIndependent t-test (men vs women with alcohol abuse):")
    print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.3f}, P-value: {p_val:.4f}")
    
    if p_val < 0.05:
        print("Result: Men with alcohol abuse show significantly greater cortical thinning than women with alcohol abuse.")
    else:
        print("Result: No significant difference in cortical thinning between men and women with alcohol abuse.")
        
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error during t-test: {e}")
```

```python
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols
import warnings

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory

try:

    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")

    "Alcohol_abuse_clinically_significant_occurring_over_a_12month_period_manifested_in_one_of_the_following_areas_work_driving_legal_or_social",
    "Subjects_sex",
    "At_least_one_MRI_scan_available"
]

missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize

for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables

# Validate sex categories (assume 0 = female, 1 = male, 2 = other)
sex_categories = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].unique()
print(f"\nUnique sex values: {sex_categories}")

# Check for invalid or out-of-range sex codes

if len(invalid_sex) > 0:
    print(f"Warning: Invalid sex codes detected ({len(invalid_sex)} rows). These entries will be removed.")
    df_clean = df_clean[(df_clean["Subjects_sex"] >= 0) & (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] <= 2)]

# Confirm valid sex groupings
sex_groups = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].value_counts()
print(f"\nSex distribution after filtering:\n{sex_groups}")

abuse_mask = df_clean["Alcohol_abuse_clinically_significant_occurring_over_a_12month_period_manifested_in_one_of_the_following_areas_work_driving_legal_or_social"] == 1
df_abuse = df_clean[abuse_mask].copy()

# Ensure we have at least 5 observations in each group
women_with_abuse = df_abuse[df_abuse["Subjects_sex"] == 0]
men_with_abuse = df_abuse[df_abuse["Subjects_sex"] == 1]

if len(women_with_abuse) < 5 or len(men_with_abuse) < 5:
    print("Error: Insufficient sample size in one or both groups with alcohol abuse. Cannot perform reliable comparison.")
    exit()

# Check if white matter integrity data exists — it must be present in the dataset
white_matter_cols = [
    "WM_Integrity_index", 
    "Fractional_anisotropy", 
    "Mean_diffusivity", 
    "Radial_diffusivity", 
    "Axial_diffusivity"
]

available_wm_cols = [col for col in white_matter_cols if col in df_clean.columns]
if not available_wm_cols:
    print("Error: No white matter integrity variable found in the dataset. Hypothesis cannot be tested.")
    exit()

# Select first available white matter metric for analysis
wm_metric = available_wm_cols[0]
print(f"\nUsing white matter integrity metric: {wm_metric}")

# Extract white matter integrity values for women and men with alcohol abuse
women_wm = women_with_abuse[wm_metric]
men_wm = men_with_abuse[wm_metric]

# Perform independent t-test comparing white matter integrity between women and men with alcohol abuse
try:
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(women_wm, men_wm, equal_var=False)
    print(f"\nIndependent t-test (women vs men with alcohol abuse):")
    print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.3f}, P-value: {p_val:.4f}")
    
    if p_val < 0.05:
        print("Result: Women with alcohol abuse show significantly lower white matter integrity than men with alcohol abuse.")

        print("Result: No significant difference in white matter integrity between women and men with alcohol abuse.")
        
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error during t-test: {e}")
```

```python
    print(f"Warning: Invalid sex codes detected ({len(invalid_sex)} rows). These entries will be removed.")
    df_clean = df_clean[(df_clean["Subjects_sex"] >= 0) & (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] <= 2)]

# Confirm valid sex groupings
sex_groups = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].value_counts()
print(f"\nSex distribution after filtering:\n{sex_groups}")

# Check for amygdala volume data — must exist in the dataset
amygdala_cols = [
    "Amygdala_volume_ml",
    "Left_Amygdala_volume_ml",
    "Right_Amygdala_volume_ml"
]

available_amy_cols = [col for col in amygdala_cols if col in df_clean.columns]
if not available_amy_cols:
    print("Error: No amygdala volume variable found in the dataset. Hypothesis cannot be tested.")
    exit()

# Select the most appropriate amygdala volume measure (prefer left/right combined or total)
if "Amygdala_volume_ml" in available_amy_cols:
    amygdala_volume_col = "Amygdala_volume_ml"
elif "Left_Amygdala_volume_ml" in available_amy_cols and "Right_Amygdala_volume_ml" in available_amy_cols:
    amygdala_volume_col = "Left_Amygdala_volume_ml"  # fallback to left if both exist
else:
    print("Error: Unable to select a valid amygdala volume column.")
    exit()

print(f"\nUsing amygdala volume metric: {amygdala_volume_col}")

# Extract amygdala volume data
amygdala_data = df_clean[amygdala_volume_col].dropna()

# Filter for individuals with clinically significant alcohol abuse (value == 1)
abuse_mask = df_clean["Alcohol_abuse_clinically_significant_occurring_over_a_12month_period_manifested_in_one_of_the_following_areas_work_driving_legal_or_social"] == 1
df_abuse = df_clean[abuse_mask].copy()

# Remove NaNs from amygdala volume in abusive group
df_abuse_clean = df_abuse.dropna(subset=[amygdala_volume_col])

# Ensure we have sufficient data per gender
male_abuse = df_abuse_clean[df_abuse_clean["Subjects_sex"] == 1]
female_abuse = df_abuse_clean[df_abuse_clean["Subjects_sex"] == 0]

if len(male_abuse) < 5 or len(female_abuse) < 5:
    print("Error: Insufficient sample size in one or both gender groups with alcohol abuse. Cannot perform reliable comparison.")
    exit()

# Extract amygdala volumes by gender
male_volumes = male_abuse[amygdala_volume_col]
female_volumes = female_abuse[amygdala_volume_col]

# Perform independent t-test to compare amygdala volume between genders with alcohol abuse
try:
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(female_volumes, male_volumes, equal_var=False)
    print(f"\nIndependent t-test (female vs male with alcohol abuse):")
    print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.3f}, P-value: {p_val:.4f}")
    
    if p_val < 0.05:
        print("Result: There is a statistically significant difference in amygdala volume between females and males with alcohol abuse.")
    else:
        print("Result: No statistically significant difference in amygdala volume between females and males with alcohol abuse.")
        
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error during t-test: {e}")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import pearsonr
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Semantic_memory_is_negatively_associated_with_age_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = ["Subjects_age_at_visit", "Memory"]

missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and ranges
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

print(f"\nAge range (min, max): {df_clean['Subjects_age_at_visit'].min()}, {df_clean['Subjects_age_at_visit'].max()}")
print(f"Memory range (min, max): {df_clean['Memory'].min():.3f}, {df_clean['Memory'].max():.3f}")

# Check for extreme outliers using IQR method
def detect_outliers_iqr(data):
    Q1 = data.quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = data.quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    return data[(data < lower_bound) | (data > upper_bound)].count(), lower_bound, upper_bound

age_outliers, low_age, up_age = detect_outliers_iqr(df_clean["Subjects_age_at_visit"])
memory_outliers, low_mem, up_mem = detect_outliers_iqr(df_clean["Memory"])

print(f"\nOutlier detection (IQR method):")
print(f"Age outliers: {age_outliers} records outside bounds [{low_age:.1f}, {up_age:.1f}]")
print(f"Memory outliers: {memory_outliers} records outside bounds [{low_mem:.3f}, {up_mem:.3f}]")

# Perform Pearson correlation between age and semantic memory
correlation_coefficient, p_value = pearsonr(df_clean["Subjects_age_at_visit"], df_clean["Memory"])

print(f"\nPearson correlation analysis (age vs semantic memory):")
print(f"Correlation coefficient: {correlation_coefficient:.4f}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value:.4f}")

if p_value < 0.05:
    print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant negative association between age and semantic memory.")
else:
    print("Conclusion: No statistically significant association between age and semantic memory.")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import f_oneway, ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Ethnicity_is_associated_with_differences_in_semant_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = ["HispanicLatino_ethnicity", "Memory"]

missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and ranges
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

print(f"\nHispanicLatino_ethnicity range (min, max): {df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].min()}, {df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].max()}")
print(f"Memory score range (min, max): {df_clean['Memory'].min():.3f}, {df_clean['Memory'].max():.3f}")

# Identify unique ethnicity groups (assuming binary or categorical grouping based on HispanicLatino_ethnicity)
# If the variable is coded as 0 (non-Hispanic) and 1 (Hispanic/Latino), we can group accordingly
ethnic_groups = df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].unique()
print(f"\nUnique ethnic groups identified: {list(ethnic_groups)}")

# Group data by ethnicity and check memory performance
grouped_data = df_clean.groupby('HispanicLatino_ethnicity')['Memory'].agg(['mean', 'std', 'count']).round(4)
print(f"\nMean Memory Performance by Ethnicity Group:")
print(grouped_data)

# Perform ANOVA test to assess overall difference across groups (if more than two groups exist)
if len(ethnic_groups) > 2:
    try:
        f_statistic, p_value_anova = f_oneway(*[df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == group]['Memory'] 
                                                for group in ethnic_groups])
        print(f"\nANOVA Test Results (across ethnic groups):")
        print(f"F-statistic: {f_statistic:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_anova:.4f}")
        
        if p_value_anova < 0.05:
            print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance across ethnic groups.")
        else:
            print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance across ethnic groups.")
            
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error during ANOVA: {str(e)}")
        print("Falling back to pairwise t-tests for two-group comparison.")
        
        # If only two groups, perform t-test
        if len(ethnic_groups) == 2:
            group0 = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == ethnic_groups[0]]
            group1 = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == ethnic_groups[1]]
            
            t_stat, p_value_t = ttest_ind(group0['Memory'], group1['Memory'], equal_var=False)
            print(f"\nPairwise T-test between groups ({ethnic_groups[0]} vs {ethnic_groups[1]}):")
            print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_t:.4f}")
            
            if p_value_t < 0.05:
                print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance between the two ethnic groups.")
            else:
                print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance between the two ethnic groups.")
                
else:
    print("Only one ethnic group present – no meaningful comparison possible.")
    
# Final assessment
print("\nNote: Given the nature of semantic memory and known neurocognitive influences, observed differences must be interpreted cautiously. Without further context on how ethnicity is defined (e.g., self-reported, genetic ancestry), results may reflect confounding sociocultural or environmental factors rather than direct biological associations.")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import f_oneway, ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Individuals_of_certain_ethnicities_show_greater_vi_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = ["HispanicLatino_ethnicity", "Race", "Subjects_age_at_visit", "Indicate_whether_the_subject_currently_is_meaningfully_impaired_relative_to_previously_attained_abilities_in_visuospatial_function"]

missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and basic statistics
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

print(f"\nHispanicLatino_ethnicity range (min, max): {df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].min()}, {df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].max()}")
print(f"Race range (min, max): {df_clean['Race'].min()}, {df_clean['Race'].max()}")
print(f"Age range (min, max): {df_clean['Subjects_age_at_visit'].min()}, {df_clean['Subjects_age_at_visit'].max()}")

# Check distribution of visuospatial impairment status (0 = not impaired, 1 = impaired)
impairment_status = df_clean['Indicate_whether_the_subject_currently_is_meaningfully_impaired_relative_to_previously_attained_abilities_in_visuospatial_function'].value_counts()
print(f"\nVisuospatial impairment status distribution:")
print(impairment_status)

# Group by HispanicLatino_ethnicity and compute mean impairment status (lower mean = better visuospatial skills)
grouped_impairment = df_clean.groupby('HispanicLatino_ethnicity')['Indicate_whether_the_subject_currently_is_meaningfully_impaired_relative_to_previously_attained_abilities_in_visuospatial_function'].agg(['mean', 'count']).round(4)
print(f"\nMean Visuospatial Impairment Status by Ethnicity Group (lower = better skills):")
print(grouped_impairment)

# Perform ANOVA to test for differences in impairment status across ethnicity groups
ethnic_groups = df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].unique()
if len(ethnic_groups) > 2:
    try:
        f_statistic, p_value_anova = f_oneway(
            *[
                df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == group][
                    'Indicate_whether_the_subject_currently_is_meaningfully_impaired_relative_to_previously_attained_abilities_in_visuospatial_function'
                ]
                for group in ethnic_groups
            ]
        )
        print(f"\nANOVA Test Results (across ethnicity groups):")
        print(f"F-statistic: {f_statistic:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_anova:.4f}")
        
        if p_value_anova < 0.05:
            print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in visuospatial impairment status across ethnic groups.")
        else:
            print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in visuospatial impairment status across ethnic groups.")
            
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error during ANOVA: {str(e)}")
        print("Falling back to pairwise t-tests for two-group comparison.")
        
        # Only proceed with t-test if exactly two groups
        if len(ethnic_groups) == 2:
            group0 = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == ethnic_groups[0]]
            group1 = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == ethnic_groups[1]]
            
            t_stat, p_value_t = ttest_ind(
                group0['Indicate_whether_the_subject_currently_is_meaningfully_impaired_relative_to_previously_attained_abilities_in_visuospatial_function'],
                group1['Indicate_whether_the_subject_currently_is_meaningfully_impaired_relative_to_previously_attained_abilities_in_visuospatial_function'],
                equal_var=False
            )
            print(f"\nPairwise T-test between groups ({ethnic_groups[0]} vs {ethnic_groups[1]}):")
            print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_t:.4f}")
            
            if p_value_t < 0.05:
                print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in visuospatial impairment status between the two ethnic groups.")
            else:
                print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in visuospatial impairment status between the two ethnic groups.")
else:
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import f_oneway, ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Semantic_memory_performance_varies_by_ethnicity_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = ["HispanicLatino_ethnicity", "Memory", "Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW"]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and basic statistics
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

print(f"\nHispanicLatino_ethnicity range (min, max): {df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].min()}, {df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].max()}")
print(f"Memory range (min, max): {df_clean['Memory'].min():.2f}, {df_clean['Memory'].max():.2f}")
print(f"MMSE score range (min, max): {df_clean['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW'].min():.2f}, {df_clean['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW'].max():.2f}")

# Check distribution of ethnicity groups
ethnic_groups = df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'].unique()
print(f"\nEthnicity groups present: {list(ethnic_groups)}")

# Compute mean semantic memory performance (Memory) by ethnicity group
grouped_memory = df_clean.groupby('HispanicLatino_ethnicity')['Memory'].agg(['mean', 'std', 'count']).round(4)
print(f"\nMean Semantic Memory Performance by Ethnicity Group:")
print(grouped_memory)

# Perform ANOVA to test for differences in memory performance across ethnicity groups
if len(ethnic_groups) > 2:
    try:
        f_statistic, p_value_anova = f_oneway(
            *[
                df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == group]['Memory']
                for group in ethnic_groups
            ]
        )
        print(f"\nANOVA Test Results (across ethnicity groups):")
        print(f"F-statistic: {f_statistic:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_anova:.4f}")
        
        if p_value_anova < 0.05:
            print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance across ethnicity groups.")
        else:
            print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance across ethnicity groups.")
            
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error during ANOVA: {str(e)}")
        print("Falling back to pairwise t-tests for two-group comparison.")
        
        # Only proceed with t-test if exactly two groups
        if len(ethnic_groups) == 2:
            group0 = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == ethnic_groups[0]]
            group1 = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == ethnic_groups[1]]
            
            t_stat, p_value_t = ttest_ind(
                group0['Memory'],
                group1['Memory'],
                equal_var=False
            )
            print(f"\nPairwise T-test between groups ({ethnic_groups[0]} vs {ethnic_groups[1]}):")
            print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_t:.4f}")
            
            if p_value_t < 0.05:
                print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance between the two ethnic groups.")
            else:
                print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in semantic memory performance between the two ethnic groups.")
else:
    print("Only one ethnicity group present – no meaningful comparison possible.")

# Examine MMSE as a potential covariate
mmse_by_group = df_clean.groupby('HispanicLatino_ethnicity')['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW'].agg(['mean', 'std']).round(2)
print(f"\nAverage MMSE Score by Ethnicity Group:")
print(mmse_by_group)

# Correlation between memory and MMSE score within each group
correlations = []
for group in ethnic_groups:
    subset = df_clean[df_clean['HispanicLatino_ethnicity'] == group]
    corr = subset['Memory'].corr(subset['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW'])
    correlations.append((group, corr))

print(f"\nCorrelation between Memory and MMSE Score by Ethnicity Group:")
for group, corr in correlations:
    print(f"Group {group}: {corr:.3f}")

# Note on interpretation
print("\nNote: Semantic memory performance is assessed using continuous measures. While the analysis tests for group-level differences, caution is advised in interpreting results due to potential confounding factors such as age, education level, comorbidities, or health disparities related to ethnicity. Without adjusting for these variables, observed differences may reflect systemic inequities rather than intrinsic cognitive variation. Additionally, the definition and measurement of ethnicity in this dataset should be interpreted carefully to avoid reinforcing biases.")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import f_oneway, ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Individuals_with_sleep_disorders_have_poorer_proce_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit",
    "Other_sleep_disorder_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit",
    "Subjects_age_at_visit",
    "Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW",
    "MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and basic statistics
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

print(f"\nSleep apnea history range (min, max): {df_clean['Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit'].min():.2f}, {df_clean['Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit'].max():.2f}")
print(f"Other sleep disorder history range (min, max): {df_clean['Other_sleep_disorder_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit'].min():.2f}, {df_clean['Other_sleep_disorder_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit'].max():.2f}")
print(f"Age range (min, max): {df_clean['Subjects_age_at_visit'].min():.0f}, {df_clean['Subjects_age_at_visit'].max():.0f}")
print(f"MMSE score range (min, max): {df_clean['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW'].min():.2f}, {df_clean['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW'].max():.2f}")
print(f"MoCA score range (min, max): {df_clean['MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education'].min():.2f}, {df_clean['MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education'].max():.2f}")

# Define procedural memory proxy: Use MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education as a proxy for procedural memory performance
# We will compare MoCA scores between individuals with and without sleep disorders

# First, define presence of sleep disorder: combine both sleep disorder indicators
df_clean['has_sleep_disorder'] = (
    (df_clean['Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit'] > 0) |
    (df_clean['Other_sleep_disorder_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit'] > 0)
)

# Recode binary variable
df_clean['has_sleep_disorder'] = df_clean['has_sleep_disorder'].astype(int)

# Group by sleep disorder status and compute mean MoCA score
mo_ca_by_group = df_clean.groupby('has_sleep_disorder')['MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education'].agg(['mean', 'std', 'count']).round(4)
print(f"\nMean Procedural Memory (MoCA) Score by Sleep Disorder Status:")
print(mo_ca_by_group)

# Perform independent samples t-test to assess difference in MoCA scores between groups
group_yes = df_clean[df_clean['has_sleep_disorder'] == 1]['MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education']
group_no = df_clean[df_clean['has_sleep_disorder'] == 0]['MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education']

# Conduct t-test assuming unequal variances
t_stat, p_value_t = ttest_ind(group_yes, group_no, equal_var=False)

print(f"\nT-test Results (with sleep disorder vs. without):")
print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_t:.4f}")

if p_value_t < 0.05:
    print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in procedural memory performance between individuals with and without sleep disorders.")
else:
    print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in procedural memory performance between individuals with and without sleep disorders.")

# Check correlation between sleep disorder presence and MMSE score (as a control for general cognition)
correlation_mmse = df_clean['MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education'].corr(
    df_clean['Total_MMSE_score_using_DLROW']
)
print(f"\nCorrelation between MoCA (procedural memory) and MMSE (global cognition): {correlation_mmse:.3f}")

# Additional note on interpretation
print("\nNote: The analysis treats MoCA_Total_Score_corrected_for_education as a proxy for procedural memory. However, MoCA is a broad cognitive screening tool that includes multiple domains, including memory, executive function, and attention. Thus, its use as a direct measure of procedural memory requires careful interpretation. Furthermore, the presence of sleep disorders may be influenced by many factors beyond their effect on procedural memory, such as medication use, lifestyle, or comorbid conditions. Without controlling for age, education, or baseline health status, observed associations may reflect confounding or selection bias. Adjustment for these variables would strengthen the validity of conclusions.")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Sex_differences_exist_in_procedural_memory_with_m_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Subjects_sex",
    "Memory"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and basic statistics
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

print(f"\nSex distribution (male = 1, female = 0):")
sex_count = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].value_counts(sort=False)
print(sex_count)

# Check for valid sex codes (assuming 1 = male, 0 = female)
valid_sex_mask = (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] >= 0) & (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] <= 1)
if not valid_sex_mask.all():
    print("Warning: Invalid sex values detected (values outside 0–1).")
    df_clean = df_clean[valid_sex_mask]

# Filter only valid sex entries (0 = female, 1 = male)
df_clean = df_clean[valid_sex_mask]

# Recode for clarity: 0 → Female, 1 → Male
df_clean["sex_group"] = df_clean["Subjects_sex"].map({0: "Female", 1: "Male"})

# Group by sex and compute mean memory score
memory_by_sex = df_clean.groupby("sex_group")["Memory"].agg(["mean", "std", "count"]).round(4)
print(f"\nMean Memory Score by Sex Group:")
print(memory_by_sex)

# Perform independent samples t-test to assess difference in memory scores between sexes
males = df_clean[df_clean["Subjects_sex"] == 1]["Memory"]
females = df_clean[df_clean["Subjects_sex"] == 0]["Memory"]

# Conduct t-test assuming unequal variances
try:
    t_stat, p_value_t = ttest_ind(males, females, equal_var=False)
except ValueError:
    print("Error: One or both groups have zero variance or insufficient sample size.")
    exit()

print(f"\nT-test Results (Males vs. Females):")
print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_t:.4f}")

if p_value_t < 0.05:
    print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in memory performance between males and females.")
else:
    print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in memory performance between males and females.")

# Optional: Check correlation between memory and age (if available)
if "Subjects_age_at_visit" in df_clean.columns:
    age_corr = df_clean["Memory"].corr(df_clean["Subjects_age_at_visit"])
    print(f"\nCorrelation between Memory and Age: {age_corr:.3f}")
else:
    print("\nNote: Age data not available for correlation analysis.")

# Note on interpretation
print("\nNote: This analysis uses 'Memory' as a proxy for procedural memory. However, without explicit validation that this variable reflects procedural memory specifically (e.g., through motor skill tasks or implicit learning paradigms), the interpretation remains speculative. Confounding factors such as hormonal influences, neuroanatomical differences, or activity patterns should be considered. Further research with validated procedural memory measures is recommended.")
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Women_with_sleep_disorders_show_worse_procedural_m_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Subjects_sex",
    "Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit",
    "Other_sleep_disorder_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit",
    "Memory"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=required_columns)

# Verify data types and basic statistics
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

# Filter for women only (female = 0, assuming 0 = female, 1 = male based on standard coding)
female_mask = (df_clean["Subjects_sex"] == 0)
if not female_mask.any():
    print("Error: No female subjects found in the dataset.")
    exit()

df_female_only = df_clean[female_mask].copy()

# Check presence of sleep disorder indicators
sleep_apnea_col = "Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit"
other_sleep_col = "Other_sleep_disorder_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit"

# Define binary sleep disorder status: either apnea OR other disorder reported (non-zero)
df_female_only['has_sleep_disorder'] = (
    (df_female_only[sleep_apnea_col] > 0) | 
    (df_female_only[other_sleep_col] > 0)
)

# Group by sleep disorder status and compute mean memory score
memory_by_disorder = df_female_only.groupby('has_sleep_disorder')['Memory'].agg(['mean', 'std', 'count']).round(4)
print(f"\nMean Memory Score by Sleep Disorder Status (Women Only):")
print(memory_by_disorder)

# Perform independent samples t-test comparing memory scores between women with and without sleep disorders
with_disorder = df_female_only[df_female_only['has_sleep_disorder']]['Memory']
without_disorder = df_female_only[~df_female_only['has_sleep_disorder']]['Memory']

# Ensure both groups have sufficient data
if len(with_disorder) == 0 or len(without_disorder) == 0:
    print("Error: One or both groups (with/without sleep disorder) are empty after filtering.")
    exit()

# Conduct t-test assuming unequal variances
try:
    t_stat, p_value_t = ttest_ind(with_disorder, without_disorder, equal_var=False)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error during t-test: {e}")
    exit()

print(f"\nT-test Results (Women with Sleep Disorder vs. Without):")
print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}, P-value: {p_value_t:.4f}")

if p_value_t < 0.05:
    print("Conclusion: There is a statistically significant difference in procedural memory between women with and without sleep disorders.")
else:
    print("Conclusion: No statistically significant difference in procedural memory between women with and without sleep disorders.")

# Optional: Check correlation between memory and age (if available)
if "Subjects_age_at_visit" in df_clean.columns:
    age_corr = df_female_only["Memory"].corr(df_female_only["Subjects_age_at_visit"])
    print(f"\nCorrelation between Memory and Age (in women): {age_corr:.3f}")
else:
    print("\nNote: Age data not available for correlation analysis.")

# Final note on validity
print("\nNote: This analysis focuses solely on women and defines sleep disorder presence based on self-reported history. Correlations may be confounded by comorbidities or age-related changes. Further validation using clinical assessments of procedural memory is recommended.")
```

```python
import seaborn as sns

# Load the cleaned dataset for visualization
file_path = "./working/filtered_Men_with_sleep_disorders_exhibit_reduced_procedura_NACC.csv"

    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns
required_columns = ["Subjects_sex", "Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit", "Memory"]

if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

male_mask = (df["Subjects_sex"] == 1)
df_male = df[male_mask].copy()

# Create binary variable for sleep disorder (based on non-zero apnea history)
df_male['has_sleep_disorder'] = (df_male["Sleep_apnea_history_reported_at_Initial_Visit"] > 0)

# Set up the plot

plt.close()
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Cerebrospinal_fluid_biomarker_levels_are_different_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Congestive_heart_failure_present",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key biomarker variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=[col for col in required_columns if col != "Congestive_heart_failure_present"])

# Verify data types and basic statistics
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

# Create binary flag for congestive heart failure presence (1 = present, 0 = absent)
df_clean['has_chf'] = (df_clean["Congestive_heart_failure_present"] > 0).astype(int)

# Filter out rows where no biomarker measurement was reported (to avoid missing data bias)
# We exclude cases where none of the biomarkers were reported
df_clean = df_clean[(df_clean["One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported"] > 0) | 
                    (df_clean["One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported"] > 0) | 
                    (df_clean["One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"] > 0)]

# Now perform t-tests for each biomarker comparing CHF+ vs CHF– groups
biomarkers = {
    "Aβ142": "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "Ptau181P": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "Ttau": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
}

results = {}

for name, col_name in biomarkers.items():
    # Extract values for CHF present and absent
    chf_present = df_clean[df_clean['has_chf'] == 1][col_name]
    chf_absent = df_clean[df_clean['has_chf'] == 0][col_name]
    
    # Skip if either group is empty
    if len(chf_present) == 0 or len(chf_absent) == 0:
        results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
        continue
    
    try:
        t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(chf_present, chf_absent, equal_var=False)
        significant = p_value < 0.05
    except Exception as e:
        results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
        print(f"Error in t-test for {name}: {e}")
        continue
    
    results[name] = {
        "t_stat": t_stat,
        "p_value": p_value,
        "significant": significant
    }

# Print results
print("\nStatistical Results for Biomarker Levels by CHF Presence:")
for biomarker, result in results.items():
    print(f"{biomarker}: T-statistic = {result['t_stat']:.4f}, P-value = {result['p_value']:.4f}, Significant? {'Yes' if result['significant'] else 'No'}")
```

```python
import pandas as pd

    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

    print("Error: Dataset not found.")
    exit()

# Ensure required columns exist
required_columns = [
    "Congestive_heart_failure_present",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",

    print("Required columns missing in dataset.")

# Filter out cases with no biomarker reports
df_filtered = df[

    (df["One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"] > 0)
]

biomarkers = ["Aβ142", "Ptau181P", "Ttau"]
markers = {
    "Aβ142": "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "Ptau181P": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "Ttau": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
}

# Set up plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

for i, marker in enumerate(biomarkers):
    data = df_filtered[markers[marker]]
    chf_group = df_filtered.groupby('has_chf')[markers[marker]].mean()
    
    # Plot mean values per group with error bars (since we don't have actual level values, only presence/absence flags)
    plt.subplot(2, 2, i + 1)
    bar_width = 0.35
    indices = [0, 1]
    bars1 = plt.bar(indices, chf_group.values, bar_width, label='CHF Present', color='skyblue')
    plt.xticks(indices, ['Absent', 'Present'])
    plt.title(f'Mean Biomarker Report Presence by CHF Status ({marker})')
    plt.ylabel('Reported (Presence)')
    plt.ylim(0, 1)
    plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
    
    # Add value labels on top of bars
    for j, val in enumerate(chf_group.values):
        plt.text(j, val + 0.01, f'{val:.1f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("./working/biomarker_presence_by_chf_status.png", dpi=300)
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Marital_status_is_associated_with_differences_in_c_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Marital_status",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key biomarker variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=[
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
])

# Verify data types and basic structure
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

# Convert marital status to categorical and verify distribution
df_clean['marital_status_cat'] = df_clean['Marital_status'].astype(str).str.strip()
print(f"\nMarital status distribution:")
print(df_clean['marital_status_cat'].value_counts(dropna=False))

# Perform t-tests for each biomarker across marital status categories
biomarkers = {
    "Aβ142": "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "Ptau181P": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "Ttau": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
}

results = {}

for name, col_name in biomarkers.items():
    # Group by marital status category and extract reported counts
    grouped = df_clean.groupby('marital_status_cat')[col_name].agg(['mean', 'count']).reset_index()
    
    # Only proceed if at least two distinct marital statuses exist
    if len(grouped) < 2:
        results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
        continue
    
    # Extract means for each group
    group_means = grouped['mean'].values
    group_sizes = grouped['count'].values
    
    # Perform t-test assuming unequal variances
    try:
        # Group by unique marital status values
        status_groups = df_clean.groupby('marital_status_cat')[col_name]
        group_data_list = []
        for status, group in status_groups:
            if len(group) >= 2:  # Need at least two observations per group
                group_data_list.append(group.values)
        
        if len(group_data_list) < 2:
            results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
            continue
        
        # Combine data from valid groups
        data1 = group_data_list[0]
        data2 = group_data_list[1]
        
        # Perform independent t-test
        t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(data1, data2, equal_var=False)
        significant = p_value < 0.05
        
    except Exception as e:
        results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
        print(f"Error in t-test for {name}: {e}")
        continue
    
    results[name] = {
        "t_stat": t_stat,
        "p_value": p_value,
        "significant": significant
    }

# Print results
print("\nStatistical Results for Biomarker Report Presence by Marital Status:")
for biomarker, result in results.items():
    print(f"{biomarker}: T-statistic = {result['t_stat']:.4f}, P-value = {result['p_value']:.4f}, Significant? {'Yes' if result['significant'] else 'No'}")
```

```python
import pandas as pd

import seaborn as sns

# Load the cleaned dataset
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load the filtered dataset from the working directory
file_path = "./working/filtered_Individuals_with_congestive_heart_failure_show_alt_NACC.csv"
try:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: The dataset file was not found at the specified path.")
    exit()

# Validate required columns for the hypothesis
required_columns = [
    "Congestive_heart_failure",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in df.columns]
if missing_columns:
    print(f"Error: Missing required columns in the dataset: {missing_columns}")
    exit()

# Check for missing values and summarize
print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:
    print(f"{col}: {df[col].isnull().sum()}")

# Drop rows with missing values in key biomarker variables
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=[
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
])

# Verify data types and basic structure
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

# Filter participants into CHF vs. non-CHF groups
df_clean["chf_group"] = df_clean["Congestive_heart_failure"].apply(lambda x: 1 if x > 0 else 0)

# Separate CHF and control groups
chf_group = df_clean[df_clean["chf_group"] == 1]
control_group = df_clean[df_clean["chf_group"] == 0]

# Ensure sufficient sample size in each group
if len(chf_group) < 5 or len(control_group) < 5:
    print("Warning: Insufficient sample size in either CHF or control group for meaningful comparison.")
else:
    # Perform t-tests for each biomarker report presence between CHF and control groups
    biomarkers = {
        "Aβ142": "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
        "Ptau181P": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
        "Ttau": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
    }
    
    results = {}
    
    for name, col_name in biomarkers.items():
        try:
            chf_values = chf_group[col_name].dropna()
            control_values = control_group[col_name].dropna()
            
            if len(chf_values) < 2 or len(control_values) < 2:
                results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
                continue
                
            t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(chf_values, control_values, equal_var=False)
            significant = p_value < 0.05
            
            results[name] = {
                "t_stat": t_stat,
                "p_value": p_value,
                "significant": significant
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            results[name] = {"t_stat": None, "p_value": None, "significant": False}
            print(f"Error in t-test for {name}: {e}")
    
    # Print results
    print(f"\nStatistical Results for Biomarker Report Presence in CHF vs. Healthy Controls:")
    for biomarker, result in results.items():
        print(f"{biomarker}: T-statistic = {result['t_stat']:.4f}, P-value = {result['p_value']:.4f}, Significant? {'Yes' if result['significant'] else 'No'}")
```

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Load cleaned data for visualization
file_path = "./working/filtered_Individuals_with_congestive_heart_failure_show_alt_NACC.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Validate and prepare data
required_columns = [
    "Congestive_heart_failure",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
]
if not all(col in df.columns for col in required_columns):
    print("Error: Required columns missing in dataset.")
    exit()

# Create binary group variable
df["chf_group"] = df["Congestive_heart_failure"].apply(lambda x: 1 if x > 0 else 0)

# Prepare data for plotting
chf_data = df[df["chf_group"] == 1][["One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported", "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported", "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"]]
control_data = df[df["chf_group"] == 0][["One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported", "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported", "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"]]

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create bar plot comparing biomarker report presence between groups
biomarkers = ["Aβ142", "Ptau181P", "Ttau"]
x_positions = np.arange(len(biomarkers))
bar_width = 0.35

plt.bar(x_positions - bar_width/2, 
        chf_data.mean(), 
        width=bar_width, 
        label='CHF', 
        color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1'],
        edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)

plt.bar(x_positions + bar_width/2, 
        control_data.mean(), 
        width=bar_width, 
        label='Control', 
        color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1'], 
        alpha=0.8, 
        edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)

plt.xlabel('Biomarker')
plt.ylabel('Mean Report Presence (0 = absent, 1 = present)')
plt.title('Mean Biomarker Report Presence in CHF vs. Healthy Controls')
plt.xticks(x_positions, biomarkers)
plt.legend(title='Group')

# Improve layout and save
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("./working/biomarker_report_presence_comparison.png", dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("Visualization saved to ./working/biomarker_report_presence_comparison.png")
```

```python
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
]

print("\nMissing values per column:")
for col in required_columns:

    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
    "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
])

# Verify data types and basic structure
print(f"\nData types:")
print(df_clean.dtypes)

# Define marital status categories: 1 = Married, 0 = Not married (or other)
df_clean["marital_group"] = df_clean["Marital_status"].apply(lambda x: 1 if x >= 1 else 0)

# Separate married vs. unmarried groups
married_group = df_clean[df_clean["marital_group"] == 1]
unmarried_group = df_clean[df_clean["marital_group"] == 0]

# Ensure sufficient sample size in each group
if len(married_group) < 5 or len(unmarried_group) < 5:
    print("Warning: Insufficient sample size in either married or unmarried group for meaningful comparison.")
else:
    # Perform t-tests for each biomarker report presence between married and unmarried groups
    biomarkers = {
        "Aβ142": "One_or_more_measures_of_Aβ142_reported",
        "Ptau181P": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ptau181P_reported",
        "Ttau": "One_or_more_measures_of_Ttau_reported"
    }

            unmarried_values = unmarried_group[col_name].dropna()

            t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(married_values, unmarried_values, equal_var=False)

            results[name] = {

            print(f"Error in t-test for {name}: {e}")
    
    # Print results
    print(f"\nStatistical Results for Biomarker Report Presence in Married vs. Unmarried Individuals:")
    for biomarker, result in results.items():
        print(f"{biomarker}: T-statistic = {result['t_stat']:.4f}, P-value = {result['p_value']:.4f}, Significant? {'Yes' if result['significant'] else 'No'}")
```
